title: Sunny and the Cockatoo Family
description: Little Sonny the quokka watches a noisy, cheerful cockatoo family settling in for the evening. A warm, funny bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Just as the afternoon was turning golden, the cockatoos arrived.

They came in a mob, white and yellow-crested, screaming and swooping and arguing with each other in the way that cockatoos always do. They landed in the big old gum tree all at once, and suddenly the whole tree seemed to be arguing.

Sunny sat safely at a distance and watched.

There was a very large cockatoo that seemed to think it should sit on the best branch. And another that disagreed. They leaned toward each other and raised their yellow crests and made extremely loud comments.

A smaller one had found a piece of bark and was chewing on it with absolute commitment. Another was hanging upside down from a branch for no apparent reason.

Two were grooming each other carefully, crest to crest, very affectionate in between all the screaming.

A tiny one — a young one, Sunny guessed — sat in the middle of all this chaos looking slightly overwhelmed. It blinked. It swayed on its branch.

Sunny understood.

But then one of the adults sidled over and groomed the young one's head gently, very tenderly, until it fluffed itself up and settled in.

Slowly, the arguments softened.

The crests went down.

The noise became quieter, and then murmuring, and then the whole tree fell into a gentle, collective cockatoo doze.

Sunny looked at them all, white and quiet in the golden tree.

He smiled.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, cockatoo family. Goodnight, noisy, wonderful, beloved bush.
